title: CXMT's fifth-generation DRAM enters mass production without EUV
subtitle: China's ChangXin Memory hit an 11.95-nanometer active-area half-pitch using quadruple patterning and claims 50 percent more dies per wafer — sidestepping the ASML lithography tools it cannot buy.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: ChangXin Memory Technologies announced at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei on September 20 that its G5 fifth-generation DRAM platform is in mass production. The process reaches an 11.95-nanometer active-area half-pitch using quadruple patterning, a capacitor aspect ratio of 45:1, and a core cell-array height reduced to 6,762 nanometers. Two 24-gigabit LPDDR5X products in 496-ball and 245-ball packages are shipping now and are already integrated into flagship Chinese smartphones.

The technical claim that matters is the yield claim: CXMT says G5 produces at least 50 percent more dies per wafer than its previous generation. If that number holds through third-party validation, it means China has closed a meaningful part of the DRAM cost-per-bit gap with Samsung, SK hynix and Micron — the three companies that share more than 95 percent of the global market — using only DUV lithography tools that are not covered by US or Dutch export controls.

DRAM is not glamorous the way frontier AI models are, but it is the substrate everything else runs on. Every LLM inference, every training run, every AI accelerator burns through high-bandwidth memory whose supply is a persistent bottleneck. A domestic Chinese source of LPDDR5X at competitive cost per bit tightens the loop between Chinese chip designs — Huawei's Ascend, the domestic GPUs — and the memory they need, and it removes one of the last export-control levers Washington had planned to lean on. Kioxia and Micron both announced HBM capacity expansions this week for the same reason: nobody is comfortable with the current concentration.

Takeaway for learners — export controls slow a competitor, they do not stop one. The interesting engineering question is always "what problem does the ban force the other side to solve, and how permanent is their solution?" Quadruple patterning to hit 12nm without EUV is a solution CXMT can now use across many generations. When you read a story about an export control this year, look for the workaround; it usually arrives inside 18 months.
